items.title: 13.9 Reactions of halides (X-) with concentrated sulfuric acid

source_refs.note: Topic 13.9, printed page 299. The printed '2HBr(s)', '8HI(s)' and '2SO2' are noted.

blocks.text: The halide ions react differently with concentrated sulfuric acid; the products and the nature of the reaction change down the group. With sodium fluoride, fumes of hydrogen fluoride are produced, NaF(s) + H2SO4(l) gives NaHSO4 + HF(g); HF is a weak reducing agent and does not react further. With sodium chloride, fumes of hydrogen chloride: NaCl(s) + H2SO4(l) gives NaHSO4 + HCl(g). With bromide, steamy fumes of hydrogen bromide and brown fumes of bromine are produced with the smell of sulfur dioxide, a redox reaction in which HBr reduces sulfuric acid to SO2 and is itself oxidised to bromine: NaBr + H2SO4 gives NaHSO4 + HBr, then 2HBr + H2SO4 gives Br2 + SO2 + 2H2O (the print writes 2SO2 and HBr(s)). With sodium iodide, fumes of hydrogen iodide, purple fumes of iodine and the smell of H2S: HI is a strong reducing agent that reduces sulfuric acid to H2S and is oxidised to I2: NaI + H2SO4 gives NaHSO4 + HI, then 8HI + H2SO4 gives 4I2 + H2S + 4H2O. The increasing reducing power of the halide ions from fluoride to iodide leads to the more complex reactions.

blocks.prompt: How does KI react with concentrated H2SO4, and what does this show about the reducing power of iodide (Quick Check 13.5a, c)?
blocks.explanation: KI + H2SO4 gives KHSO4 + HI, and the hydrogen iodide then reduces the acid: 8HI + H2SO4 gives 4I2 + H2S + 4H2O, seen as purple iodine vapour and the rotten-egg smell of hydrogen sulfide. Reducing sulfur from +6 all the way to -2 shows that iodide is a very strong reducing agent, far stronger than bromide (which reaches only SO2) or chloride (which does not reduce the acid at all).

items: Conc. H2SO4 displaces HX from every sodium halide (NaX + H2SO4 gives NaHSO4 + HX); F- and Cl- stop there, Br- goes on to Br2 + SO2 (brown fumes, SO2 smell), I- to I2 + H2S (purple fumes, H2S smell): reducing power rises down the group.
